title: Subsurface Properties of Si Microholes Fabricated by Nanosecond UV Laser Beam
content: Translucent Si solar cells fabricated by a nanosecond ultraviolet (ns UV) laser have shown promise for emerging building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPVs) applications, such as windows, facades, skylights, and greenhouses [1, 2]. The use of a high-power laser beam offers fast and scalable production, which is limited in conventional micromachining techniques based on high-vacuum dry etching processes. However, this approach can introduce unintended artifacts due to the local heating effects of the laser beam on the Si substrate.
